segments.text: [soft, slow, warm voice] [softly] Sit in a way that lets the spine feel tall without becoming rigid. Soften the jaw and the small muscles around the eyes.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Bring gentle attention to the space between the eyebrows. There is no need to cross the eyes, strain, or search for a special sensation.

[soft, slow, warm voice] [soft distant waves lapping] If imagery helps, imagine an indigo lighthouse resting behind the forehead. Its beam turns slowly across a quiet inner sea, asking nothing from the horizon.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Feel one natural inhale... and one natural exhale. Let the point of attention remain light, as though a feather could land there without being held.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Thoughts may cross the beam like birds at night. There is no need to follow them or frighten them away. Notice the crossing, then return to the lighthouse.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [thoughtfully] The Ajna point is being used here as a focus for attention and imagination. You do not need to see colours, feel energy, or make anything happen.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Notice the darkness behind the eyelids. Perhaps it is flat, grainy, colourful, or changing. Let the indigo image remain optional within that wider space.
[soft, slow, warm voice] If pressure builds in the forehead, broaden attention to the whole face. Relax the eyes, feel the breath, then return only if the focus feels comfortable.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [faint distant waves lapping] For a little while, rest with the small point and the wide darkness together... a lighthouse with plenty of ocean around it.
[soft, slow, warm voice] When attention wanders, let the return be unremarkable. No alarm, no self-criticism. The beam simply completes another quiet circle.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [reassuringly] You may notice clarity, sleepiness, restlessness, or nothing in particular. The practice is the gentle returning, not the production of an experience.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Begin widening attention. Include the forehead... the face... the throat... the chest... and the contact points beneath your body.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Let the imagined lighthouse grow distant while sounds in the room become clear again. Notice how inner focus and ordinary surroundings can share the same map.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [softly] Take an easy breath. Move your hands, soften your gaze, and open your eyes when ready. Let the small blue light remain only as a memory.
